A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FoundationGait, with matching core methods and experiments, and their supplied pages are readable. v1 includes two supplementary pages; v2 ends at the references and omits that material despite retaining supplementary-material references. This document-level omission is assessed below.

before.justification: v1 reports original pretraining, recognition and healthcare evaluations, along with part-aware training, architecture and cross-modality ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds DroneGait evaluations, data-diversity and head-initialization controls, baseline results and inference timings.

M1.justification: Section 3.2, Algorithm 1 and Equations (1)-(3) retain the teacher-student architecture, EMA updates, part splitting and reassembly, InfoNCE objective and downstream adaptation procedure. Height-only shifting is newly clarified, without evidence that the underlying procedure changed.

E1.justification: v2 adds DroneGait evaluation under previously unseen UAV viewpoints, covering mid- and high-pitch views with normal, bag and clothing conditions (Table 6(c)). The original pretraining sources and recognition and healthcare tasks remain. WebGait-1M is a subsample of existing coverage.

E2.justification: v2 removes the supervised GaitSet, GaitPart and DeepGaitV2 source-target comparisons from Table 3. It adds GaitSSB-0.13B throughout recognition and healthcare comparisons, AP3D/PSTA/PiT/BigGait/BiggerGait on CCPG, and GaitGL/GaitTR on RA-GAR (Tables 4-5). Comparator membership changes substantially.

E3.justification: The part-aware ablation changes from 0.03B in v1 Table 12 to 0.13B in v2 Table 6(a). v2 also adds large-model GaitLU-1M pretraining, matched-size data subsampling, scratch-versus-linear-probe head initialization, and an FP32 inference-timing protocol. Original main training schedules and dataset splits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds Grad-CAM analysis across model sizes, unseen-UAV generalization tests, matched-size diversity controls and head-initialization analysis. It revises the part-granularity ablation and removes the CNN-versus-ViT replacement experiment from v1 Table 14. These materially change the questions investigated and supporting analyses.

E5.justification: v2 Table 2(d) newly reports inference times averaged over 20 runs after 30 warm-ups. Neither version reports corresponding repeated-seed accuracy estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests. This is a limited addition to repeated-measurement reporting.

E6.justification: The headline 48.0% Gait3D and 64.5% OU-MVLP results and existing fine-tuning scores remain unchanged. v2 adds substantial baseline, DroneGait, data-diversity, initialization and timing results, replaces the part-aware ablation with different-size-model results, and removes supervised transfer and ViT results. Table 6(a)'s 66.5 mAP entry also creates ambiguity because Table 3 reports 66.5 as Rank-5 for the matching configuration.

T1.justification: The core pretraining mathematics in Equations (1)-(3) is unchanged. The supplied v2 omits the supplementary triplet and cross-entropy loss definitions given in v1 Equations (4)-(5). Neither version supplies formal scaling theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v2 qualifies the novelty claim as vision-based gait understanding, replaces scaling-law claims with empirical scaling trends, and describes the unchanged headline results as self-supervised rather than zero-shot. The central contribution of a scalable model spanning recognition and healthcare remains.

C2.justification: v2 expands the mechanism explanation to argue that post-backbone part pooling occurs too late, attributes large-model failures on GaitLU-1M to limited diversity, and interprets new initialization controls. It acknowledges the gap to BiggerGait and adds an RGB limitation, while removing the ViT-failure discussion and the earlier part-granularity tradeoff interpretation.

D1.justification: v2 omits v1's supplementary task-head architectures, downstream loss details, controlled cropping/masking instructions and parsing-silhouette distance-fusion procedure. It adds height-shift clarification, inference hardware/settings and fine-tuning time/hardware disclosures. The abstract also changes code/model access wording from forthcoming to available, although actual availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: A new related-work subsection discusses GaitFM, GaitDynamics and PathoFM and explicitly distinguishes FoundationGait's vision-based scope. DroneGait and additional RGB comparator references are added, while scaling-law and several face-related citations are removed. Most existing gait and healthcare positioning is retained.

P1.justification: The main section progression remains intact. v2 rewrites selected motivation and results paragraphs, standardizes self-supervised/scaling-trend terminology, condenses healthcare discussion and renames the concluding section. The supplementary and ethics sections present in v1 are absent.

P2.justification: v2 changes from a two-column layout to a single-column format and extensively reorganizes displays. Configuration, recognition, healthcare and ablation tables become grouped panels; scaling figures are redrawn and reordered, Grad-CAM images are added, captions expand, and supplementary Figures 5-7 disappear.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens evaluation through unseen-domain tests, matched-size diversity controls and broader comparisons, while better qualifying its claims. However, it loses important reproducibility details and the ViT failure analysis, and the new part-aware ablation contains unresolved metric-label ambiguity. These material benefits and losses prevent a reliable net quality judgment from the supplied PDFs.
